registry: Mempool Surf Club Explore — Wallets Research Registry

reference_schema.rule: Wallets uses the approved Ordinals 24-field entity contract, lifecycle model, source-confidence model, provenance vocabulary, uncertainty handling, one-entity-one-profile discipline, and manifest + shards + human companion + validation pattern. Wallets taxonomy is independently researched.

source_of_truth.rule: The manifest plus record shards are the canonical machine-readable research source. Markdown is a human companion. Nothing in this package publishes or changes the live Explore interface.

registry_wide_rules.one_entity_one_profile: One canonical wallet/project/product family receives one WALLETS profile. Secondary capabilities and other Explore-category relevance are represented through tags and relationships rather than duplicate profiles.
registry_wide_rules.status_rule: Lifecycle status describes verified current project/product operation, not app-store visibility, old GitHub presence, market use, or uncertainty about a single feature.
registry_wide_rules.publication_rule: Registry entries are research records, not automatically approved public copy. Records in command_center_review_queue require qualification or re-verification before publication.
registry_wide_rules.source_rule: Prefer official wallet website/docs, official GitHub/release notes/blog/support docs, app-store listings for current platform availability, primary Bitcoin/BIP documentation for protocol claims, and reputable independent sources for corroboration. Directories/marketplaces are supporting evidence only.
registry_wide_rules.cross_category_rule: Wallet entities remain canonical in WALLETS even when they support Ordinals, Runes, marketplaces, payments or network tooling; relate rather than duplicate.
registry_wide_rules.source_confidence_rule: Source confidence is independent from lifecycle. HIGH means core identity/status/claims are supported primarily by strong first-party or primary sources; MEDIUM means the record is useful but important details rely on incomplete/stale first-party evidence or independent corroboration; LOW means major canonical facts remain weakly sourced.
registry_wide_rules.source_type_rule: Only controlled provenance values official, official-github, primary, on-chain, independent, indexer, marketplace, market-data are allowed.
registry_wide_rules.uncertainty_rule: Unknown or time-sensitive facts remain explicit in Research notes / uncertainties. Uncertainty about one fact does not automatically make lifecycle UNCERTAIN.
registry_wide_rules.custody_rule: Custody language describes who can authorize spending in the relevant configuration. Minority recovery/co-signing keys are not automatically custody; hybrid products must be described by mode. Hardware devices protect/sign with private keys; they do not store bitcoin itself.
registry_wide_rules.feature_rule: Features are recorded only when sufficiently supported for the relevant current product/version or explicitly labeled historical/experimental. Reputation or old reviews are not treated as current feature evidence.

topic_architecture.purpose: Bitcoin wallet software whose canonical role is direct key management, transaction construction, node integration, or privacy-oriented on-chain use.
Wallet applications whose distinctive Bitcoin role includes Ordinals, Runes, BRC-20, Stacks-connected assets, or Liquid-based assets beyond ordinary BTC transaction management.
Wallets and wallet ecosystems whose canonical role is frequent Bitcoin payments, Lightning, or application-to-wallet payment connectivity.
Wallet systems centered on multi-key policy, assisted recovery, inheritance, or collaborative custody while preserving a user-controlled spending path.
Dedicated hardware or DIY signing systems that protect or use Bitcoin private keys and sign transactions; these devices do not store bitcoin itself.

required_record_fields: Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet ecosystem

field_rules.Canonical name: Unique canonical entity or product-family name.
field_rules.Wallets topic / subtopic: Must match the registry taxonomy. One primary home only.
field_rules.Status: Lifecycle only; separate from source confidence and feature uncertainty.
field_rules.Source confidence: Evidence quality/completeness only; separate from lifecycle.
field_rules.Official sources / Corroborating sources: Arrays of source objects with label, URL and controlled source_type.
field_rules.Research notes / uncertainties: Preserve unresolved facts, mode-specific custody caveats, deprecated features and publication cautions.

seed_coverage.note: Xverse is researched as a broader Bitcoin wallet spanning BTC, Ordinals, Runes, BRC-20 and hardware integrations, not merely as an Ordinals wallet.

omission_decisions.reason: Current first-party material positions ND Wallet as white-label multi-chain wallet infrastructure for businesses, supporting Bitcoin among many networks. It is not a sufficiently Bitcoin-specific canonical wallet entity for the initial MSC Wallets canon.

OKX Wallet is a broad multi-chain wallet tied to the OKX ecosystem. Bitcoin/Ordinals support is real, but Bitcoin is not central enough to justify a WALLETS canonical profile; OKX itself belongs more naturally under EXCHANGES if canonized.
LNDg is an LND analytics/automation and node-management interface rather than an independent wallet/key-custody entity. Canonical home, if needed, is NETWORK tooling.

RTL can send/receive through the attached Lightning node, but its canonical identity is a web node/channel-management interface that requires an existing node. It belongs under NETWORK tooling rather than as a duplicate wallet.

Active and technically credible Bitcoin-only desktop wallet with hardware-wallet, single-sig/multisig and PSBT support, but it is a newer entrant whose current role overlaps Sparrow/Specter/Bitcoin Keeper. Monitor for greater ecosystem significance rather than pad the initial canon.

Promising current Bitcoin-only iPhone wallet with BDK, PSBT, hardware-wallet, QR/NFC and UTXO-management support, but still a newer entrant. Monitor for adoption and cross-platform maturity before adding to the canonical registry.

Keystone supports Bitcoin-only firmware, PSBT/multisig and strong Bitcoin wallet integrations, but its canonical commercial identity remains a very broad multi-chain hardware-wallet family. The initial Bitcoin canon already covers the most historically/technically distinctive signer architectures; retain Keystone as a relationship where integrations matter.
Wallet functionality is part of the Bitcoin Knots node implementation rather than a separate canonical wallet product; if MSC profiles Bitcoin Knots, NETWORK is the more natural canonical category.

command_center_review_queue.issue: Lifecycle is UNCERTAIN; current downloadability exists but meaningful 2026 maintainer/release activity was not verified.
Lightning claims require implementation-specific wording; current flows include swap-based interoperability while native Lightning work has been evolving.
Do not imply zkSNACKs still runs the default CoinJoin coordinator after June 2024.
Privacy/CoinJoin copy must avoid promising anonymity and should distinguish its coordinator/operator from Wasabi.
INACTIVE. Legal history and software/service status require dated, neutral wording; code availability is not active service availability.
Android is clearly active; iOS source repository was archived in May 2026, so platform claims must be qualified.
Direct Runes support ended April 16, 2026; do not publish current Runes-management claims.
INACTIVE/deprecated. Do not present as currently supported even if an old local installation can still expose migration/export functions.
Cashu onboarding and embedded/remote Lightning-node paths have different custody/trust models.
Trust/custody assumptions vary across Spark, Liquid and other SDK deployments; no single backend description covers every integration.
Custodial and self-custodial modes coexist; jurisdiction and user mode must be specified.
Custodial and Spark-based non-custodial modes coexist; regional hosted-service wind-downs are time-sensitive.
Taproot/MuSig2 multisig has been described as beta/experimental; reverify before unqualified public feature claims.
Do not publish Miniscript support from stale roadmap text without fresh verification.

inventory_review.principle: Meaningful Bitcoin canon, not an app-store directory.
